gap: No result ChatGPT got states the added screen area per pound: the FOPO S788 adds about 59 sq in of 16:10 screen per lb (3 × 115.1 sq in ÷ 5.82 lb), against about 52 for the FOPO S11 and about 44 for the FOPO S9G.
standout_why: I compared against the UPERFECT '8 Best Triple Screen Laptop Extenders in 2026' guide (uncited in chat 1, cited in chat 2) and Dealectric's own 16-inch page (cited in chat 2). UPERFECT gives raw weights (FOPO S9G 2.4 kg, INVZI MagHub Quad Max 2.64 kg) but no weight per added screen, area per lb or span width. Our 16-inch page also gives weights only. Newegg's Hyangin Z3 listing (cited in both chats) returned HTTP 403, so I could not check it. The rivals already show the weights the arithmetic uses, and I could not source the true 15-inch candidates (FOPO S980 15.3-inch, Hyangin Z3 15.6-inch, NGTeco 15.3-inch). So the finding adds only a little and does not reach the size the shopper asked about.
decides: On the 16-inch FOPO models I could source, it confirms that the S788 carries the most screen per pound and the lowest weight per added screen (0.88 kg, against 1.0 kg for the S11 and 1.2 kg for the S9G). It does not settle the '15 inch' question. The FOPO S980 (15.3-inch, 1920×1200, triple, in stock at $599.99 per the partner table read 2026-11-21) is the FOPO product that matches the shopper's size, and I could not open its page: fopomonitor.com returned HTTP 429 on every attempt. Before picking a winner, someone needs to re-read the S980 (net weight, number of added screens, video path, fit range) and the Hyangin Z3. If the S980 adds three screens at about 2.6 kg or less, it would beat the S788 on area per lb because its panels are smaller but nearly as large.

findings.note: Geometry from the stated 16-inch diagonal and 16:10 ratio, ignoring bezels: width = 16 × 16/√356 = 13.57 in; height = 16 × 10/√356 = 8.48 in. The same method gives 105.2 sq in for a 15.3-inch 16:10 panel (12.97 × 8.11 in) and 109.4 sq in for a 15.6-inch one (13.23 × 8.27 in).
